questions.q: What did Monbiot witness around Brazilian gold mines?
a: Indigenous cultures collapsing and disease killing a fifth of a tribe
Rain forests recovering faster than scientists had predicted
Miners and local tribes forming a lasting partnership
Wild animals adapting easily to the new industrial landscape
questions.why: Lesson 1 says 20 percent of the Yanomami died as mining brought disease and upheaval.

questions.q: How does rewilding differ from conservation, according to the summary?
a: Conservation still controls nature by favoring chosen species
Conservation works only in oceans, while rewilding works on land
Rewilding requires constant human management of every species
Rewilding is simply another word for protecting a single habitat
questions.why: Lesson 2 says conservation is another form of control that can create imbalance.

questions.q: What is the one active step humans should take to start rewilding?
a: Bring back large animal species that once lived there
Remove all predators so smaller animals can recover
Plant fast-growing trees across the whole area
Fence the land off so no people can enter it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says restoring large animals kick-starts the recovery of an ecosystem.

questions.q: Why are large animals so important to a rewilding project?
a: They keep ecosystems lively and create habitats for other species
They eat the pests that would otherwise destroy all plant life
They move nutrients from the ocean onto the land
They discourage people from returning to abandoned areas
questions.why: Lesson 3 gives wild boars digging mini-habitats as an example of this effect.

questions.q: Why can't humanity simply return to a hunter-gatherer way of life?
a: There are too many people for the Earth to feed that way
Modern laws forbid anyone from living off the land
Hunter-gatherers destroyed most of the world's wildlife
The necessary skills have disappeared completely
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the population is now far too large for that lifestyle to work.
